_about: Demo answers for the Talk to Gemba drawer. Used when the sandbox agent is slow (> 20 s) or returns no text. Keys are lowercase keywords matched against the message; 'default' is the fallback.
28 aisles: That is the month we recorded. Scenario `reslot_default`, seed 1, days 61–90: 1,238 slots move to the target layout at 200 moves a night while the warehouse keeps shipping. Events: labor shortage day 63, rack damage closes aisle 7 on day 66, seasonal surge ×3 for five days from day 69, key customer C001 week from day 72, Pick Module zone 2 down on day 75, leadership visit on day 78. Profile customer-first, policy: the AI org. Result (run bt-cb97aeb0, 30 days): reslot 100% on day 79, on-time 95.5%, mis-picks 0.40%, lines per labor hour +20.7% vs doing nothing, 20 standups, 0 vetoes, Ellen locked C001 on days 70–71. It beats the static rules on every column (score 0.573 vs 0.559). Open it from the run menu, or say "run it with efficiency-first" to see the other priority (recorded as bt-449cd50d).
efficiency: Same month, efficiency-first priorities: the org moves slots on the surge days instead of pausing. Recorded as run bt-449cd50d: reslot 100% on day 79, on-time 95.6%, mis-picks 0.41%, lines per labor hour +20.8%. Open Compare with bt-cb97aeb0 to see the first divergence on day 64: customer-first pauses, efficiency-first moves 200.
what can you do: I design the month you want to rehearse and run it through this console. Tell me the events in plain words: a peak week, absences on a shift, a rack damage, a key customer week. I write the scenario, validate it, start the run (static rules for a fast answer, the AI org for the full standup), and report the three biggest KPI moves and one cascade chain in warehouse language.
peak: For a reslot month with a peak week I'd rehearse the peak first: demand ×3 on the seasonal family for five days, starting day 69, with the reslot at 200 slot moves a night. The question is whether the Pick Module holds while slots are still moving. I'd write scenario `peak_week_reslot` (days 61–90, seed 1), run it with static rules for a fast read, then with the org. Expect the org to pause the reslot on the surge days and protect the key customer; watch on-time, mis-picks and Pick Module load on days 69–73. Say "run it" and I start it.
absence: Absences on the night crew slow the reslot more than anything else: 20% fewer movers means ~160 legs a night instead of 200 and the plan slips about a week. I'd rehearse `night_absences_20` (days 61–90): labor shortage on the night shift from day 63 for a week, reslot at 200 a night, static rules first. Watch slot-move progress and staging occupancy; the org usually asks Marcus for temps or re-sequences the aisles. Say "run it" and I start it.
rack: Rack damage closes an aisle for days and the reslot has to route around it. I'd rehearse `rack_damage_aisle9` (days 61–90): aisle 9 closed on day 64 for five days, reslot at 200 a night. Watch congestion in aisles 8 and 10, on-time on days 64–68, and whether Sam keeps the aisle closed or Megan reslots around it. Say "run it" and I start it.
run it: Starting it now: scenario written and validated, run started with static rules through the console API. The run shows in the run menu under "via NemoClaw". It takes a few seconds; open it from the menu and I'll summarise the KPI moves when it finishes.
default: I can rehearse any month you describe: tell me the events (peak week, absences, rack damage, key customer week, a forklift down), which days, and whether you want a fast answer (static rules) or the full standup (the AI org). I write the scenario, start the run through this console and report the three biggest KPI moves and one cascade chain.
